title: Click "Create an account"
paras: Opens the sign-up form, for a family member using GoldenDose for the first time.
The "Create your family account" form appears.
alt: Sign in screen with the Create an account link circled
aside: Already have an account? Skip to click 8, Sign in.

title: Click "Your name" and type it
paras: Your name appears in the app ("Hello, Priya") and in alert messages.
Move on to the mobile number.
alt: Create account form with the Your name box circled
aside: Example used in this guide: Priya Sharma, Kamala's daughter.

title: Click "Mobile number" and type it
paras: SMS and WhatsApp alerts about missed doses are sent to this number.
Move on to the email.
alt: Create account form with the Mobile number box circled
aside: Include the country code, for example +91.

title: Click "Email" and type it
paras: Your email is how you sign in. Family members invite each other by email too.
Move on to the password.
alt: Create account form with the Email box circled
aside: One account per email address.

title: Click "Password" and choose one
paras: Protects the account. At least 8 characters. It's stored scrambled, never as you typed it.
Click Create account.
alt: Create account form with the Password box circled
aside: A shorter password is refused with the message "Choose a password of at least 8 characters."

title: Click "Create account"
paras: Creates your account and signs you in on this phone.
"Hello, Priya". Her list is empty, with a box to add the first person she looks after.
alt: Create account form with the Create account button circled
aside: If the email already has an account, the app says so and suggests signing in.

title: Click "Sign out"
paras: Signs this phone out of the account. It's always at the top right.
Back to Sign in. Next, Priya signs in again, as you would on another day.
alt: Hello, Priya screen with the Sign out link circled at the top right
aside: On your own phone you can stay signed in.

title: Click "Email" and type it
paras: The email you signed up with.
Move on to the password.
alt: Sign in screen with the Email box circled
aside: Capital letters in the email don't matter.

title: Click "Password" and type it
paras: Proves it's you. The dots hide what you type.
Click Sign in.
alt: Sign in screen with the Password box circled
aside: Forgot it? Ask the main caregiver to invite your new account.

title: Click "Sign in"
paras: Checks the email and password. If either is wrong, it says "Email or password is wrong."
"Hello, Priya". No one is on her list yet: next, she adds her mother, Kamala.
alt: Sign in screen with the Sign in button circled
aside: You stay signed in on this phone until you sign out.

title: Click "Their name" and type it
paras: The name of the person you look after, as they like to be called. Their phone greets them with it.
Click Add person.
alt: The Their name box circled
aside: Example: Kamala. You can add more people later, such as both parents.

title: Click "Add person"
paras: Adds Kamala to your list. You become her main caregiver.
Kamala's setup opens: four short steps.
alt: The Add person button circled

title: Check: "Set up Kamala"
paras: Kamala's own setup, step by step: she's added, then her first medicine, her phone, and how you're told.
Click Add a medicine.
alt: The setup steps circled
aside: You can stop at any time and come back from Kamala's page.

title: Click "Add a medicine"
paras: Step 2 of the setup. Opens the form for Kamala's first medicine. Keep the strip or prescription next to you.
The "Add a medicine for Kamala" form.
alt: Kamala's page with the Add a medicine button circled
aside: After saving, the setup comes back, ready for the next step.

title: Click "Medicine name" and type it
paras: The only required box. Shown in large letters on Kamala's screen and alarm.
Move on to the strength. Example: Calcium.
alt: Add a medicine form with the Medicine name box circled
aside: Left empty, saving shows "Enter the medicine name."

title: Click "Strength" and type it
paras: The dose, such as "500 mg". Shown next to the name and read aloud.
Move on to the instruction.
alt: Add a medicine form with the Strength box circled
aside: Optional, but it helps tell similar medicines apart.

title: Click "Instruction" and type it
paras: Read aloud to Kamala when the alarm rings. Mention the colour and when: "Take one orange tablet with water".
Move on to what it's for.
alt: Add a medicine form with the Instruction box circled
aside: The colour in the instruction helps people who recognise tablets by look rather than name.

title: Click "What it's for" and type it
paras: What the doctor said this medicine is for, such as "Bone strength". Kamala's app shows it under the name and reads it aloud.
Move on to the time.
alt: The What it's for box circled
aside: Type a common name such as Glycomet or Telma and GoldenDose suggests what it's usually for. Always go by what the doctor said.

title: Click the time and set it
paras: When the alarm rings every day. Set the hours, minutes and AM or PM.
The time is set. Add more times for medicines taken more than once a day.
alt: Add a medicine form with the time box circled
aside: In this guide the time is set a couple of minutes ahead, so the alarm rings during the guide.

title: Click "Add another time"
paras: Adds a second time, for medicines taken twice a day (or more, up to 12 times).
A new time row appears, ready to set.
alt: Add a medicine form with the Add another time button circled
aside: Each time gets its own alarm and its own card on Kamala's Today screen.

title: Click "Remove"
paras: Deletes a time you don't need. At least one time always stays.
That row disappears. Back to one time.
alt: Two time rows, with the second row's Remove button circled
aside: Calcium in this guide is taken once a day, so the extra time is removed.

title: Click "Take or choose a photo"
paras: Opens the camera or photo library. Photograph the strip or tablet: the photo replaces the drawing on Kamala's screen and alarm.
Your photo shows in the square preview. It's uploaded when you save.
alt: The Take or choose a photo button circled
aside: Optional but recommended: people recognise medicine by how it looks. This guide skips the photo and uses the drawing instead.

title: Click a shape: "Oval"
paras: Sets the shape of the pill drawing, used when there's no photo: Round, Oval or Capsule.
The chosen shape gets a green border, and the preview changes.
alt: Shape choices with Oval circled
aside: Choosing Capsule adds a second colour, for two-colour capsules.

title: Click a colour: "Orange"
paras: Sets the pill drawing's colour. Choose the real tablet's colour, so it matches what Kamala holds.
The preview turns into an orange oval tablet.
alt: Colour choices with Orange circled
aside: Nine colours: white, cream, yellow, orange, pink, red, blue, green and brown.

title: Click "Add medicine"
paras: Saves the medicine. Kamala's phone picks it up within a minute.
Back to Kamala's setup: 1 medicine added. Next, her phone.
alt: The Add medicine button circled at the bottom of the form
aside: If something's missing, a message explains what to fix, such as "Enter the medicine name."

title: Click "Get a connection code"
paras: Step 3 of the setup. Makes a 6-digit code to connect Kamala's phone, so she never needs a password.
The code appears, with numbered steps to follow on Kamala's phone.
alt: Kamala's phone section with the Get a connection code button circled
aside: Use this for a first phone, a new phone, or a bedside tablet.

title: Read the steps for Kamala's phone
paras: Open the browser on Kamala's phone, type the address shown, then the 6 digits. The code works once, for 15 minutes.
Pick up Kamala's phone. Priya's setup waits: Waiting for Kamala's phone to connect.
alt: The connection code box circled: open the address on Kamala's phone and type the 6-digit code
aside: Expired or already used? Click Get a new code.

title: Click the code box and type the 6 digits
paras: Links this phone to Kamala. The box is extra large so the digits are easy to see.
Click Connect.
alt: Welcome to GoldenDose screen with the Code box circled
aside: A short code shows "Type all 6 numbers of the code." A wrong or expired one shows "That code didn't work."

title: Click "Connect"
paras: Connects the phone. It's remembered from now on. This tap also switches on the alarm sound.
"Good evening, Kamala" and today's medicines in time order.
alt: Welcome screen with the code typed and the Connect button circled
aside: Browsers only allow sound after one tap. If the app is reopened, a yellow bar asks for one tap.

title: Check: the setup says Connected
paras: Back on Priya's phone, without touching anything: the setup turns green by itself. Kamala's phone is connected.
Click Finish.
alt: The Connected line on Kamala's page circled
aside: Kamala's phone shows it too, at the bottom of her list: Connected to your family, with Priya's name.

title: Click "Finish"
paras: Closes the setup. Everything Kamala needs is ready.
Kamala's page: today's doses, her medicines, and her phone, Connected.
alt: The Finish button circled
aside: Step 4, how you're told about missed doses, is covered in Part E.

title: Click "Read aloud"
paras: Speaks the medicine's name, strength and instruction, for when reading is hard.
The phone speaks. The screen stays the same.
alt: Kamala's Today screen with a Read aloud button circled
aside: Every card has a Read aloud button. Cream cards say "Not taken yet": late, but she can still tap Taken.

title: When the alarm rings, click "Taken"
paras: Records the dose as taken, with the time, and stops the alarm. Take the pill first, then tap.
A green "Well done" screen.
alt: Yellow alarm for Calcium 500 mg with the Taken button circled
aside: The alarm fills the screen, shows the pill, chimes and reads the instruction. Unanswered, it rings again every 5 minutes; after 30 minutes the family is told.

title: "Well done" confirms it
paras: A big green tick and the time it was taken, for 2.5 seconds.
Back to Today, or straight to the next alarm if another dose is due at the same time (here: Vitamin C).
alt: Green Well done screen: Taken at 10:26 pm
aside: Clear confirmation removes the doubt "did that work?"

title: Click "Skip this dose"
paras: Records the dose as skipped, for when told not to take it today. The alarm stops.
Back to Today. The card says "Skipped at…", and the family sees it in History.
alt: Yellow alarm for Vitamin C with the Skip this dose button circled
aside: Skip is smaller and lower than Taken, so it's hard to press by mistake.

title: Pressed by mistake? Click "Undo"
paras: Cancels "Taken" or "Skipped". Works for 5 minutes after the tap.
The card goes back to "Due now" with a Taken button. The alarm waits 5 minutes before ringing again.
alt: Green Calcium card with the Undo button circled
aside: After 5 minutes, Undo disappears and the record is final.

title: Click "Taken" on the card
paras: The same as the alarm's button, from the Today screen. A second tap within a second is ignored.
"Well done", then the card turns green.
alt: Calcium card marked Due now with the Taken button circled
aside: A dose can be marked from one hour before its time. Further ahead, the card has no Taken button.

title: The green card means "done"
paras: A tick and "Taken at 10:26 pm". Later, one glance answers "did I take it?"
Back to the family app, to see what Priya sees.
alt: Green Calcium card circled: Taken at 10:26 pm, with Undo
aside: Taps made without internet are kept on the phone and sent automatically later.

title: Click "← All people"
paras: Goes back to the list of everyone you look after. Back links are always at the top left.
The people list: Kamala, with ✓ Phone connected.
alt: Kamala's page with the All people back link circled
aside: Opening a page again always shows the latest information.

title: Click "Kamala" again
paras: Opens her page with up-to-date information, including what she just did on her phone.
Kamala's page, with today's doses and their status.
alt: People list with Kamala's card circled
aside: Reloading the page (Cmd + R) also refreshes it.

title: Check today's status
paras: Each dose with a label: green "Taken" with the time, grey "Skipped", red "Missed" (an alert was sent), yellow "Due now", or "Later".
Calcium shows "Taken 10:26 pm" and Vitamin C shows "Skipped", exactly as Kamala tapped.
alt: Today's list with the Calcium row circled, showing Taken 10:26 pm
aside: This guide was made in the evening, so earlier demo doses show as Missed.

title: Click "Last 7 days"
paras: Shows every recorded dose for the past week, to spot patterns or answer the doctor.
History, newest day first, with "4 of 5 taken" for each day.
alt: Kamala's page with the Last 7 days link circled
aside: Yesterday in the demo data shows a missed Vitamin D3.

title: Click "← Kamala"
paras: Returns to Kamala's page from history.
Kamala's page.
alt: Last 7 days page with the Kamala back link circled
aside: The browser's Back button works too.

title: Click "How you're told about missed doses"
paras: Opens your alert choices and the invite form. It's at the bottom of the person's page.
The "Alerts and family" page.
alt: Kamala's page with the How you're told about missed doses card circled
aside: The card's second line shows your current choices, such as "SMS, WhatsApp, App".

title: Click a checkbox: "SMS"
paras: Turns SMS alerts on or off for you. Tick any mix of SMS, WhatsApp and app notification. Each family member chooses their own.
The tick disappears. Nothing is saved until you click Save.
alt: Alerts and family page with the SMS checkbox circled
aside: Alerts are sent 30 minutes after a dose was due and not taken. In the test version they appear in the Terminal, not on phones.

title: Click "Save"
paras: Saves your alert choices for this person.
A green "Saved" appears above the button.
alt: Alerts form with the Save button circled
aside: Choices are per person: Priya gets WhatsApp and app alerts for her father, and all three for her mother.

title: Click "Their email" and type it
paras: The email of a family member to invite, such as Priya's sister Meera. They need their own GoldenDose account first.
Choose what they can do.
alt: Invite family form with the Their email box circled
aside: Only the main caregiver sees the Invite family section.

title: Click "What can they do?"
paras: Opens a list of two roles. Helper: see and change medicines. Main caregiver: also invite others.
Pick one (Helper is already chosen), then click Invite.
alt: Invite form with the What can they do? dropdown circled
aside: Both roles can choose their own alerts.

title: Click "Invite"
paras: Links that person to Kamala, so they can see her medicines and get alerts too.
A green confirmation appears.
alt: Invite form with the Invite button circled
aside: No account with that email? The message says "Ask them to sign up first."

title: The invitation worked
paras: "Meera Iyer can now see Kamala's medicines." Kamala now has more than one caregiver.
Next time Meera signs in, Kamala appears in her list.
alt: Green message circled: Meera Iyer can now see Kamala's medicines
aside: One caregiver can look after several people, and one person can have several caregivers.

title: Click "← Kamala"
paras: Returns to Kamala's page, to manage her medicines.
Kamala's page, with her medicines listed.
alt: Alerts and family page with the Kamala back link circled
aside: The back link always names the page it returns to.

title: Click a medicine: "Amlodipine"
paras: Opens it to change any detail (name, strength, instruction, times, photo, shape, colour), then Save changes.
The "Change Amlodipine" form, filled in with its current details.
alt: Medicines list with Amlodipine circled
aside: Changes reach Kamala's phone within a minute.

title: Click "Stop Amlodipine"
paras: Starts stopping a medicine the doctor has stopped. It's at the bottom of the form, and it asks first.
A question: "Stop Amlodipine?" with "Yes, stop it" and "Keep it".
alt: Change Amlodipine form with the Stop Amlodipine button circled
aside: Stopping is reversible: open the medicine again and save to restart it.

title: Click "Keep it" (or "Yes, stop it")
paras: Keep it cancels. Yes, stop it ends the reminders. Past records are kept, so history still makes sense.
Keep it: the question closes. Yes, stop it: back to Kamala's page, without that medicine.
alt: Stop Amlodipine question with the Keep it button circled
aside: This guide chooses Keep it, so the demo data stays the same.

title: Click "Tablets in hand now" and type it
paras: Starts the medicine meter. Count the tablets you have; a line shows how many days they last and when to order.
Click Save changes.
alt: The Change Amlodipine form with the Tablets in hand now box circled
aside: Count again whenever you buy more. Tablets in each dose: use 0.5 for half a tablet.

title: Click "Save changes"
paras: Saves the count. The medicine now shows about how many days are left.
Kamala's page. The medicine shows the days left and an Order by date. When it's time to order, a Running low box appears and the family gets a message.
alt: The Save changes button circled
aside: The meter says "about": it counts by the schedule, so recount now and then.

title: Click "Language, hospital and chemist"
paras: Opens the settings for Kamala's app language, her emergency hospital and your chemist.
The Language, hospital and chemist page.
alt: Kamala's page with the Language, hospital and chemist card circled
aside: Any family member who looks after Kamala can change these.

title: Choose a language: "हिन्दी (Hindi)"
paras: Kamala's app changes to this language: buttons, messages and Read aloud. Nine languages, including English.
Fill in the hospital.
alt: The language list circled
aside: Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Telugu, Tamil, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam or English. Medicine names show as you type them.

title: Click "Hospital phone number" and type it
paras: The hospital Kamala's emergency button offers to call, as well as the ambulance (108).
Move on to your chemist.
alt: The Hospital phone number box circled
aside: Use the hospital's emergency (casualty) number if it has one.

title: Click "Chemist's WhatsApp number" and type it
paras: Your own chemist. When a medicine runs low, you can send them the list on WhatsApp in one tap.
Click Save.
alt: The Chemist's WhatsApp number box circled
aside: Include the country code: +91 for India.

title: Click "Save"
paras: Saves the language, hospital and chemist. Kamala's phone shows the new language straight away.
A green "Saved" appears.
alt: The Save button circled

title: Click "← Kamala"
paras: Back to Kamala's page.
The Running low box, now with an Order on WhatsApp button.
alt: The back link to Kamala circled

title: Click "Order on WhatsApp"
paras: Opens WhatsApp with the order already written to your chemist. Nothing is sent until you press Send.
Check the message in WhatsApp, then send it.
alt: The Order on WhatsApp from Sharma Medical button circled
aside: It uses your own WhatsApp, so it costs nothing.

title: Click "इमरजेंसी" (Emergency)
paras: Tells every family member at once, on every channel, with a map link if the phone shares its location.
The emergency screen, in Kamala's language.
alt: Kamala's app in Hindi with the Emergency button circled
aside: The family is told the moment it is pressed.

title: Click "City Hospital को फ़ोन करें" (Call City Hospital)
paras: Calls the hospital. "Call ambulance 108" calls the ambulance, and "Nearest hospitals" opens the map.
When help has come, or if it was a mistake: I'm OK.
alt: The emergency screen with the Call City Hospital button circled
aside: A web page can't dial by itself, so Kamala taps to call.

title: Click "मैं ठीक हूँ" (I'm OK)
paras: Tells the family Kamala is OK. They should still call to check.
Back to Today.
alt: The I'm OK button circled

title: Check: the emergency banner
paras: A red banner at the top of Kamala's page: when the button was pressed, and when she said she's OK.
Call Kamala to check, even after "I'm OK".
alt: Kamala's page on Priya's phone with the red emergency banner circled

title: Click "Doctor visit report"
paras: Opens a report of the last 30 days: what was taken, missed and skipped, for each medicine.
The report. Choose 30, 60 or 90 days.
alt: The Doctor visit report card circled
aside: Take it to every doctor's visit.

title: Click "Print or save as PDF"
paras: Opens the print screen. Choose Save as PDF to keep a copy, or print it for the doctor.
A tidy page with every medicine, what it's for, and how often it was taken.
alt: The Print or save as PDF button circled
aside: Download spreadsheet is just below it, for anyone who likes Excel.

title: Click "Share summary on WhatsApp"
paras: Opens WhatsApp with a short summary ready to send to your family or the doctor.
Choose who to send it to. Nothing is sent until you press Send.
alt: The Share summary on WhatsApp button circled
aside: It uses your own WhatsApp, so it costs nothing.

title: Click "← Kamala"
paras: Back to Kamala's page.
Kamala's page, with Records and reports.
alt: The back link circled

title: Click "Prescriptions"
paras: Opens the prescriptions page: photos and PDFs from the doctor, kept in one place.
The Prescriptions page.
alt: The Prescriptions card circled
aside: Only Kamala's family can see them.

title: Click "Take a photo"
paras: Opens the camera. Take a clear photo of the whole prescription.
The photo uploads, and boxes for the doctor and date appear.
alt: The Take a photo button circled
aside: Or click Choose a photo or PDF for one you already have.

title: Click "Doctor" and type the name
paras: Who wrote the prescription, such as "Dr. S. Rao".
Move on to the date.
alt: The Doctor box circled

title: Click "Date on the prescription" and set it
paras: The date written on the prescription.
Click Save details.
alt: The date box circled
aside: A note is optional: "Sugar review, next visit in 3 months".

title: Click "Save details"
paras: Saves the doctor and date with the photo.
The prescription in the list, with Open, Edit details and Remove.
alt: The Save details button circled

title: Click "← Kamala"
paras: Back to Kamala's page.
Kamala's page.
alt: The back link circled

title: Click "Change history"
paras: Opens every change to Kamala's medicines and settings: who made it, when, and why.
The Change history page.
alt: The Change history card circled
aside: Brothers and sisters sharing the care always know what changed.

title: Read the change history
paras: Newest first: the prescription just added, Kamala's language, the tablets counted, the medicine added.
Below it: the medicine list on any past date.
alt: The change history list circled
aside: If the main caregiver switches on approval, a helper's medicine changes wait here for their OK.

title: Click "← Kamala"
paras: Back to Kamala's page.
Kamala's page.
alt: The back link circled

title: Click "Setup check"
paras: Shows what's set up and what's still to do, such as a photo for every medicine.
The Setup check page.
alt: The Setup check card circled

title: Check what's left to set up
paras: A green tick for each thing that's done. Anything not done says how to fix it; tap it to go there.
Finish the rest when you have a moment.
alt: The setup list circled
aside: It updates by itself as you add photos, counts and numbers.

title: Click "← Kamala"
paras: Back to Kamala's page.
Kamala's page.
alt: The back link circled

title: Click "Ask"
paras: Opens Ask GoldenDose: ask about Kamala's medicines in plain words, in any language.
The Ask panel, with ready-made questions.
alt: The Ask button circled
aside: Answers come only from Kamala's records. It never gives medical advice: for doses or symptoms, ask the doctor.

title: Click "What is each medicine for?"
paras: Asks one of the ready-made questions.
The answer appears in a moment.
alt: The question circled

title: Read the answer
paras: Each medicine and what it's for, from Kamala's records.
Type another question, or close the panel.
alt: The answer circled
aside: Try: "How did she do this week?" or "Is anything running low?"

title: Click "Close"
paras: Closes the Ask panel.
Kamala's page.
alt: The Close link circled

title: Click "Health records"
paras: Opens Kamala's health records: blood reports, tests the doctor wants repeated, blood pressure, weight, sugar, questions for the doctor and the next visit.
The Health records page.
alt: The Health records card circled
aside: GoldenDose reminds you; the doctor decides.

title: Check the reminders
paras: GoldenDose noticed Kamala takes medicines for blood pressure and diabetes, and suggests regular checks.
Next, add her latest blood report.
alt: The reminders circled
aside: Suggestions like these stay in the app; they're never sent as messages.

title: Click "Add a blood report"
paras: Opens the form for a new report: its date, the lab, a photo or PDF, and the numbers that matter.
The Add a blood report form.
alt: The Add a blood report button circled
aside: Keep the paper report next to you.

title: Choose a test: "HbA1c"
paras: Picks the test from a list of common ones. The unit fills in by itself.
Type the result.
alt: The Test list circled
aside: Another test? Choose Another test… at the bottom and type its name.

title: Click "Result" and type it
paras: The number on the report, here 8.2.
Type the range printed on the report.
alt: The Result box circled

title: Click "Range on the report: from" and type it
paras: The low end of the normal range printed next to that result on the report, here 4.
Type the high end.
alt: The range box circled
aside: Always the lab's own range: GoldenDose never uses ranges of its own.

title: Click "to" and type it
paras: The high end of the printed range, here 5.6.
Click Save report.
alt: The second range box circled
aside: Add another result for each test that matters, such as creatinine or cholesterol.

title: Click "Save report"
paras: Saves the report and its results.
Back to Health records, with the report and a reminder.
alt: The Save report button circled
aside: A photo or PDF of the report can be added on the same form.

title: Check: outside the printed range
paras: 8.2 is above the range printed on the report (4–5.6), so GoldenDose asks: has Kamala's doctor seen it?
Share it with the doctor, then mark it as seen.
alt: The reminder circled
aside: It stays on the list until you mark it. The family is also sent one message.

title: Click "Share with the doctor"
paras: Opens WhatsApp with the results written out, ready to send to the doctor or the family.
Choose who to send it to. Nothing is sent until you press Send.
alt: The Share with the doctor button circled

title: Click "Doctor has seen it"
paras: Records that the doctor has seen the report. The reminder goes away.
The report shows ✓ Doctor has seen it.
alt: The Doctor has seen it button circled

title: Choose how often to repeat it: "Every 3 months"
paras: As the doctor said. GoldenDose works out when the next test is due.
The next due date appears. You're reminded a week before, and if it's overdue.
alt: The Repeat list circled

title: Choose "Remind me to check blood pressure": "Every week"
paras: How often the family should take a BP reading.
Add the target the doctor gave.
alt: The reminder list circled

title: Type the doctor's target
paras: The top and bottom numbers the doctor gave, here 140/90.
Click Save.
alt: The target boxes circled
aside: Only the doctor's target: GoldenDose then tells you when a reading is above it.

title: Click "Save"
paras: Saves the BP reminders and target.
A reminder: No blood pressure reading yet.
alt: The Save button circled

title: Click "Top number" and type it
paras: The top number from the BP machine, here 162.
Type the bottom number.
alt: The Top number box circled

title: Click "Bottom number" and type it
paras: The bottom number, here 95.
Click Save reading.
alt: The Bottom number box circled
aside: A pulse can be added too.

title: Click "Save reading"
paras: Saves the reading with the time.
The latest reading, and a reminder.
alt: The Save reading button circled

title: Check: above the doctor's target
paras: 162/95 is above the target the doctor gave (140/90). GoldenDose suggests sharing the readings with the doctor.
Next, a question for the doctor.
alt: The reminder circled

title: Click "New question" and type it
paras: Anything to ask at the next visit, such as whether a tablet can be taken with dinner.
Click Add.
alt: The New question box circled
aside: Anyone in the family can add questions, whenever they think of them.

title: Click "Add"
paras: Adds it to the list. Questions print with the doctor visit report.
The question in the list, with Answered and Remove.
alt: The Add button circled
aside: After the visit, click Answered and note what the doctor said.

title: Click "Weight (kg)" and type it
paras: Today's weight, here 58.5. Choose a reminder to weigh regularly if you like.
Click Save.
alt: The Weight box circled
aside: A change of 5% or more in about a month is flagged as worth telling the doctor.

title: Click "Save"
paras: Saves the weight. Blood sugar works the same way, just below.
The latest weight.
alt: The Save button circled

title: Type your lab's WhatsApp number
paras: The lab you use, so home sample collections can be booked in one tap.
Click Save.
alt: The lab's WhatsApp number box circled
aside: Many labs in India collect samples at home.

title: Click "Save"
paras: Saves the lab.
A Book a home collection button appears, for the tests the doctor wants repeated.
alt: The Save button circled

title: Click "Book a home collection"
paras: Opens WhatsApp with a message to the lab listing the tests, asking for a day and time.
Check it in WhatsApp, then send it.
alt: The Book a home collection button circled
aside: It uses your own WhatsApp, so it costs nothing.

title: Click "← Kamala"
paras: Back to Kamala's page.
Kamala's page.
alt: The back link circled

title: Click "Sign out" when finished
paras: Signs this phone out. Do this on a shared or borrowed phone.
Back to the Sign in screen. Kamala's phone stays connected.
alt: Change Amlodipine page with the Sign out link circled at the top right
aside: On your own phone you can stay signed in.
